## Investigación con agentes (Claude Opus 5.5; puede contener errores)
# Zaporizhzhia NPP offsite power: research notes (compiled 2026-10-06, no forecast)

**Source access:** All three researchers got HTTP 402 errors from iaea.org, so none of us read the IAEA pages directly. The IAEA quotes below come from search snippets and from outlets citing the IAEA, and should be checked against the original pages. Metaculus FAQ "definitions" was not checked separately. It only matters as the fallback for "credible sources".

## 1. What the resolution source shows

- **Latest IAEA update we could confirm: Update 368, 25 Sep 2026.** https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/update-368-iaea-director-general-statement-on-situation-in-ukraine
  - It says: "Currently the plant is receiving off-site power through its sole remaining power line, the 330 kilovolt (kV) Ferosplavna-1 line."
  - Diesel fuel stocks are "continu[ing] to decline". "Four of the site's 20 generators will now start automatically following a loss of off-site power, while the remaining available units will require manual connection by plant staff." The same detail is reported by NEI: https://www.neimagazine.com/news/znpp-revises-emergency-power-strategy/
- **An Update 369 dated about 2 Oct 2026 is UNVERIFIED.** A search tool named it but returned no content.
  - Vedomosti on 2 Oct 2026 quoted Grossi: ZNPP "currently relies on a single 330 kV line". It also cited 10 disconnections since June and critically low diesel. https://www.vedomosti.ru/business/news/2026/10/02/1233830-grossi-prizval-sotrudnichat
- **Update 367, 17 Sep 2026:** "Since June alone, the ZNPP has suffered 10 losses of offsite power, marking 26 since the conflict began in 2022." https://www.iaea.org/newscenter/pressreleases/update-367-iaea-director-general-statement-on-situation-in-ukraine
  - The counts disagree across sources. Al Jazeera and RIA called the 20 Aug event the 27th.
- **750 kV Dniprovska line:** down since 24 Mar 2026.
  - On 26 Jun 2026 it was described as "repaired but cannot be connected yet", because of substation damage with no near-term fix. https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/06/26/8041243/
  - Update 368's "sole remaining" wording means it was still unavailable as of 25 Sep.
  - So ZNPP has no redundancy: any cut to Ferosplavna-1 is a total loss of offsite power.

## 2. Recent news and current status

- **20 Aug – 7 Sep 2026: about 18 days on diesel.** Ferosplavna-1 was cut by military activity north of the Dnipro.
  - On 28–29 Aug about 10 days of fuel remained, which is the regulatory minimum. https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/29/ukrainian-nuclear-power-plant-without-external-power-for-over-a-week
  - The line was repaired during the 7th IAEA-brokered local ceasefire (5–7 Sep) and reconnected on the evening of 7 Sep. https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/zaporizhzhia-reconnected-to-external-power-after-18-days ; https://www.ans.org/news/2026-09-09/article-8377/zaporizhzhia-restores-offsite-power-following-iaeabrokered-local-ceasefire/
- **Earlier in August 2026: losses on 1, 4 and 8 Aug.** https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2026-09/news/outages-rising-zaporizhzhia-power-plant
- **19, 20 and 27 Sep 2026: drone strikes damaged transformers at the Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant (ZTPP).**
  - The IAEA calls these transformers "vital" for ZNPP's offsite power. Ferosplavna-1 reportedly runs through the ZTPP switchyard.
  - Grossi is negotiating an 8th local ceasefire for repairs, to start "very soon". No date had been set as of 3 Oct. https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-economy/4170677-iaea-reports-damage-to-transformers-near-zaporizhzhia-npp-seeks-truce-for-repairs.html
- **3–5 Oct 2026: AMBIGUOUS whether ZNPP is still connected.**
  - Vedomosti (3 Oct) says the ZTPP equipment "is receiving power from emergency sources". It does not say ZNPP itself lost offsite power. https://www.vedomosti.ru/politics/news/2026/10/03/1234016-oborudovanie-povrezhdeno
  - On 5 Oct, Rosatom's Likhachev said a ZTPP transformer was hit about two weeks earlier. He said the IAEA was notified on 30 Sep and that terms for a truce are being negotiated.
    - Some AI summaries of Interfax and Izvestia render this as ZNPP running on diesel for two weeks. That reading is UNCONFIRMED and conflicts with the IAEA and Vedomosti wording. https://www.interfax.ru/world/1120353 ; https://iz.ru/2178775/2026-10-05/postradavshikh-pri-atake-vsu-na-proizvodstvennye-zdaniia-zaes-net-stantciia
  - We found no IAEA or Energoatom report of a new total loss of offsite power after 7 Sep. **Best reading: ZNPP is connected via Ferosplavna-1 as of about 2–5 Oct, but this is not confirmed.** The next IAEA update needs checking.
- **NucNet, 2–5 Oct:** diesel is still low, fewer generators may be kept on automatic standby, and resupply is held up by fighting. https://www.nucnet.org/news/zaporizhzhya-considering-reduction-in-number-of-emergency-diesel-generators-on-standby-10-5-2026
- **5 Oct 2026:** an overnight attack damaged a lab building about 200 m from Units 4–5 and a radioactive-waste facility, according to the Russian side. https://www.vedomosti.ru/politics/news/2026/10/05/1234203-vsu-atakovali-obekt
- **29 Sep 2026:** Rosatom says it has a phased restart plan, to be used only "after a reduction of military risks". All six units have been in cold shutdown since 2022. https://www.vedomosti.ru/business/news/2026/09/29/1232765-plan-zapuska-zaes
- **Scheduled before 17 Oct:** only the possible 8th repair ceasefire, with no date. We found no ZNPP-specific peace deal or event.
  - IAEA updates have been roughly weekly (11, 17 and 25 Sep), so 1–2 more updates are likely before 17 Oct.
- **Prediction markets:** we found no offsite-power market on Polymarket, Manifold or Metaculus.
  - Polymarket has only "Explosion at ZNPP by …" markets. We saw them on 6 Oct 2026 but have no prices or volumes for them.

## 3. Base rates (rough; durations partly from memory and only partly verified)

- **Total losses of offsite power:** about 26–27 since 2022.
  - About 5 in 2022, 3 in 2023, possibly 1 in 2024 (uncertain), and 3 in 2025.
  - About 15 in 2026, mostly April–August.
- **Long outages:**
  - 23 Sep – 23 Oct 2025: about 30 days. https://www.world-nuclear-news.org/articles/external-power-restored-to-zaporizhzhia-nuclear-plant-after-30-days
  - 20 Aug – 7 Sep 2026: about 18 days.
  - Most other 2026 events lasted from minutes to about 15 hours.
- **Share of days without any offsite power, estimated:**
  - Since March 2022: about 3–4% (about 55–60 of about 1,677 days).
  - Last 12 months (Oct 2025 – Oct 2026): about 10–11% (about 38–40 days), from about 17 events.
- **Single line:** ZNPP has been on one line for most of 2025 and since 24 Mar 2026. Before the war it had 10 lines.
- **Run of days without a loss:** in Apr–Aug 2026 the gaps between losses were often only days. The current run since 7 Sep is about 4 weeks, assuming the ZTPP damage has not cut ZNPP's supply (see the ambiguity above).
- **Restoration times:** the 2025 and 2026 long outages each needed an IAEA-brokered local ceasefire. These took about 2–4 weeks to arrange and carry out.

## Flags

- Everything before the question opened is background only. The question is decided solely by the status on or around 17 Oct 2026.
- The main uncertainty is whether the ZTPP transformer damage from 19–27 Sep has affected ZNPP's own supply. Check the newest IAEA update (Update 369 or later).

criterios: This question resolves YES if, according to the most recent IAEA "Update ... – IAEA Director General Statement on Situation in Ukraine" (or equivalent IAEA statement) published on or before October 17, 2026 that describes the plant's power status as of October 17, 2026, the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) is connected to at least one external (offsite) high-voltage power line supplying electricity from the grid on that date. It resolves NO if the plant is reported to have suffered a complete loss of all offsite power on October 17, 2026 and is relying solely on emergency diesel generators on that date. IAEA updates are published at https://www.iaea.org/ukraine-conflict . If no IAEA statement explicitly addresses the plant's offsite-power status on exactly October 17, 2026, resolution will use the status reported as of the closest available date on or around October 17, 2026 from the IAEA, or from other credible sources (https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions).
letra_pequena: A single connected offsite line is sufficient for YES; the plant need not have full redundancy. Brief interruptions earlier in the day that are restored before the end of October 17, 2026 (local Ukraine time) do not by themselves force a NO if the plant is reported connected to the grid as of that date. If the IAEA ceases publishing status updates and no credible source reports the plant's offsite-power status for any date within one week of October 17, 2026, the question is annulled.
razonamientos:
(a) **Time left:** 11 days, from October 6 to October 17, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** YES. The latest status the research could substantiate has ZNPP receiving grid power through one offsite line, though its status after the recent nearby transformer damage is not fully confirmed.

(c) **Reference class:** The research estimates ZNPP lacked offsite power on roughly 10–11% of days over the past year. That is a rough base rate, and the current single-line connection makes the next 11 days unusually vulnerable.

(d) **NO scenario:** The remaining line is cut, and damage or fighting prevents its restoration by the end of October 17.

(e) **YES scenario:** The line stays connected, or any interruption is repaired by the end of October 17.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** One connected offsite line is enough for YES. An earlier interruption that day does not force NO if grid power is restored by day’s end; if no statement covers the exact date, the closest credible status report is used.

I give the connected status quo substantial weight, while allowing for the recent frequency of outages and the possibility of a prolonged repair.

Probability: 82%

(a) **Time left:** 11 days, from October 6 to October 17, 2026.

(b) **Status quo:** The best available reading is that ZNPP remains connected through the single 330-kV Ferosplavna-1 line, though its current status is not fully confirmed. If nothing changes, the outcome is YES.

(c) **Reference class:** ZNPP appears to have lacked all offsite power on roughly 10–11% of days over the past year. That recent rate is more relevant than its lower rate across the full war.

(d) **NO scenario:** The sole connected line is damaged or disconnected, and repairs cannot restore it by October 17; the plant relies entirely on diesel generators.

(e) **YES scenario:** Ferosplavna-1 stays connected, or any interruption is repaired by the end of October 17.

(f) **Resolution technicality:** One supplying offsite line is enough for YES. A brief outage earlier that day does not force NO if power is restored by day’s end; if no report addresses October 17 exactly, the closest credible status report may decide it.

The single-line vulnerability and recent long outages make NO a substantial risk, but the apparently connected status quo remains the stronger forecast.

Probability: 85%

**(a) Time left:** 11 days, until 17 Oct 2026. Resolution depends on the IAEA update covering that date, likely published around 17–23 Oct.

**(b) Status quo:** The plant appears connected via its single 330-kV Ferosplavna-1 line.
- IAEA Update 368 (25 Sep) said power was coming through this "sole remaining" line.
- On 2 Oct, Grossi said the plant "currently relies on a single 330 kV line."
- Some Russian-media summaries suggest a two-week diesel period. These conflict with the IAEA wording. A real total loss would almost certainly have been announced loudly by the IAEA, so the status quo is YES.

**(c) Reference class:** Share of days on which ZNPP had no offsite power.
- Since 2022: about 3–4% of days.
- Last 12 months: about 10–11% of days.
- Conditions are now especially fragile. There is no redundant line. Drone strikes damaged transformers at the nearby thermal power plant (ZTPP) on 19, 20 and 27 Sep; the IAEA calls these "vital" for the plant's power. Repairs are pending a ceasefire. Total losses happened often between April and August 2026.
- Given that, the risk on a given day is somewhat above the 12-month average. Long outages (18–30 days) make a loss in the next 11 days especially likely to still be ongoing on 17 Oct.

**(d) NO scenario:** Further strikes, or failure of the already damaged ZTPP transformers, cut Ferosplavna-1 in the next 11 days. Repair then needs another IAEA-brokered local ceasefire, which takes weeks to arrange. The plant is on diesel on 17 Oct.

**(e) YES scenario:** Ferosplavna-1 stays up, as it has since 7 Sep. Alternatively, a brief outage occurs and is restored before 17 Oct. Possibly the 8th repair ceasefire happens and stabilizes the transformers.

**(f) Technicalities:**
- A single connected line is enough for YES.
- An interruption on 17 Oct that is restored the same day still counts as YES.
- If no IAEA statement covers exactly 17 Oct, the closest reported date is used, which favors the status quo.
- The main hidden risk is that the plant is already disconnected and the IAEA has not yet reported it. I judge this unlikely.

I estimate about a 15% chance the plant is on diesel on 17 Oct, giving roughly 85% for YES.

Probability: 85%
